query: One More Night {Sister Amaranth wants you in for "one more night, for observation". You feel completely fine and have three things due tomorrow.|One more night again. Sister Amaranth has started leaving your boots on the far side of the ward.|The bed by the window has your name on the slate in ink. "One more night," says Sister Amaranth, not as a question.} Stay the night {You stay. You sleep through two bells and the breakfast trolley and wake up much better than "completely fine" turned out to be. Your three things are now late.|You stay. She was right, irritatingly; you sleep like a dropped stone. Your essay, unwritten, waits.|You stay without arguing. Sister Amaranth notices, and gives you the good tonic, and a look that might be respect.} Argue your case {You make a short, true, convincing case. She looks at you over her spectacles. "Go," she says. "Come back if it swells. Don't come back if it doesn't."|You tell her the true version of how fine you are, with the limp left in. She respects that and lets you go.|She lets you go with a tonic in your pocket and instructions you'll follow later, when you understand them.} {She listens to every word, then points at the bed. You lie down. You don't remember falling asleep.|"No," says Sister Amaranth, which was always going to be the answer, and she says it while doing something else.|She lets you argue to the end, then writes "argued" on your slate, under your name.} Step out through the dark {When her lamp turns, you step into the shadow behind the screen and out of the shadow by the door. In the morning there's a note on your desk in square handwriting. It says "Next time, ask."|You step out of the ward and into your own room's corner in one breath. You get your three things done. Sister Amaranth, of course, knows.|Shadow to shadow, past the beds, out. Your essay is finished by midnight. At breakfast Sister Amaranth puts a tonic by your plate without a word.}
